tagline: An old trade path over the Hoosac, motored since 1914.
intro: Out of Williamstown and through North Adams, Route 2 climbs the Hoosac Range by a steep, curving road to the hairpin turn and on up to Whitcomb Summit, 2,272 feet. On the far side it drops down the Cold River to the Deerfield and follows the water east, past the mill towns, to the Connecticut and the Millers.

The line is older than the road. It began as a Native American trade route linking the Atlantic tribes with those of upstate New York, and when it opened to automobiles on October 22, 1914 it was New England's first scenic road. Some of the souvenir shops and tourist cottages of that era are still open.

moments.title: The Hairpin Turn
moments.text: The road doubles back on itself on the west face of the range, with a lookout over North Adams and the Taconic Mountains beyond.

moments.title: Bridge of Flowers
moments.text: A 1908 trolley bridge over the Deerfield that nobody could tear down because it carried the water main, so in 1929 the women's clubs planted a garden on it.

moments.title: French King Bridge
moments.text: The road crosses the Connecticut 140 feet up on a 1932 steel arch named for French King Rock, which still shows in the middle of the river.

sources.label: Western Massachusetts Scenic Byways, Mohawk Trail
